meta.title: Five-Day Asset Inventory: Two Planes to One Catalog

views.label: Two planes
views.note: The metastore plane and the workspace plane are collected separately and cover different things.

views.label: Day 3: cross-references
views.note: Cross-references turn two counts into blockers and shared dependencies that plan the wave.

views.label: Decision to sign-off
views.note: Every asset gets an owner and a retire/defer/migrate decision before the catalog is considered done.

cards.title: Two planes, two collections
items: Metastore plane holds catalogs, schemas, tables, grants — collected once, account-wide
Workspace plane holds jobs, clusters, dashboards, secrets and object ACLs — collected per workspace
Unity Catalog grants are not the whole permission story: object ACLs live in a separate API

cards.title: Day 3 is the one people skip
items: Counts alone don't tell you sequencing — cross-references do
A shared SQL warehouse or cluster policy means those assets cannot land in different waves
dbxmig crossrefs finds broken references deterministically, no model involved

cards.title: What ships to wave planning
items: Every asset class carries a count, an owner, and a retire/defer/migrate decision
Shared-reference clusters are the direct input to wave design
An inventory without Day 3 is 60% complete and often believed finished
